lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The target role is unclear.
items.because: The résumé combines diesel mechanics, logistics operations, product management, an MBA, and student ventures.

items.says: Separate targeted versions should be created for product, operations, strategy, or mechanical roles.
items.because: One general résumé dilutes the evidence most relevant to each function.

items.says: The strongest product evidence is diluted by operational and mechanical experience.
items.because: Product applications should prioritize Harbor Payments and the product projects.

items.says: The experience section is not in reverse chronological order.
items.because: The 2018–2023 Crestline role appears before the 2024 Harbor Payments internship.

items.says: The MBA, internship, and ongoing student-project dates need to be checked for clear compatibility.
items.because: Their overlapping dates raise chronology questions.

items.says: The career transition involving the current diesel-mechanic role is unexplained.
items.because: Recruiters may wonder why the current job is mechanical rather than product- or business-related.

items.says: Coastal Marine Services should be separated as Additional Experience in a product- or business-focused version.
items.because: Its relevance to those target roles is not clear.

items.says: Coastal Marine Services needs more prominence and technical detail in a mechanical or industrial-operations version.
items.because: That experience would be central for those target roles.

items.says: The breadth of the Crestline role is not communicated clearly enough.
items.because: Its bullets show program management, process improvement, stakeholder management, and vendor ownership beyond an analytical title.

items.says: Ownership claims in the Harbor Payments entry should reflect an intern's actual responsibility level.
items.because: Company-wide launches and roadmap decisions can overstate intern ownership.

items.says: Academic projects should be distinguished clearly from professional employment.
items.because: Recruiters evaluate MBA projects differently from operating work experience.

items.says: The section order should be targeted to the intended role.
items.because: A product version should prioritize relevant experience and projects over education and less relevant work.

items.says: Metric conventions should be standardized across the résumé.
items.because: Percentage points, relative increases, time periods, modeled savings, user types, and rollout scope are not always distinguished consistently.

items.says: The résumé may be too dense for one page without tighter prioritization.
items.because: The Harbor Payments bullets are dense and overlapping.

items.says: A summary may be needed to clarify the career transition and target function.
items.because: The current sequence from operations and an MBA to product work and then diesel mechanics lacks a clear narrative.

items.says: The LinkedIn URL should be a clickable, professional link rather than a generic or incomplete display.
Clarify whether the MBA has been completed.
items.because: A degree ending in June 2025 should no longer appear ongoing after that date.

items.says: Clarify whether the under-five-day dry-dock time is an average, target, maximum, or improvement.
items.because: Without a baseline or definition, the achievement is difficult to evaluate.

items.says: Add the number of rebuild jobs completed if substantial.
items.because: Fleet size alone does not show individual throughput.

items.says: Explain dry-dock time for audiences outside marine operations.
items.because: The term may not be understood by the target audience.

items.says: The bullet is primarily a responsibility statement rather than an accomplishment.
items.because: It describes maintenance and record logging without an outcome.

items.says: Add measurable scale such as systems, vessels, inspections, or records.
State the inspection, compliance, or regulatory outcome.
items.because: The bullet does not say whether inspections passed, were on time, or met a requirement.

items.says: “Owned” is too vague.
items.because: The bullet does not explain what ownership involved.

items.says: The meeting description focuses on logistics rather than business impact.
items.because: It only says the monthly meeting discussed the scorecards.

items.says: Add the number of carriers, regions, managers, or shipments covered.
items.because: The current bullet lacks scale.

items.says: Explain what decisions or performance improvements resulted from the scorecards.
items.because: The bullet is not yet a strong accomplishment.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period and baseline for the 30% reduction.
items.because: A percentage reduction is more credible when its timeframe is known.

items.says: Add context for “pick errors” in versions aimed at general business readers.
items.because: The term may be clear only to logistics employers.

items.says: Define S&OP on first use for generalist recruiters.
Clarify the forecast-error metric and what was being forecast.
The 12-quarter duration may be removable if space is limited.
items.because: The result is more important than the duration.

items.says: The bullet may be too dense because it combines several accomplishments.
items.because: Tool rollout, SOP redesign, training, and vendor negotiations may not all need to remain together.

items.says: Clarify how the 1,800 saved hours were calculated and validated.
Make the causal link between the telematics contract and driver-hour savings clearer.
items.because: Their relationship is not fully clear.

items.says: Clarify the candidate's personal role in the onboarding redesign.
items.because: It is unclear whether the solution was designed personally, jointly, or as a contribution.

items.says: Clarify that the single verification step remained within required compliance and risk controls.
items.because: The change may raise compliance or risk questions.

items.says: Verify that all 2,300 merchants were in the measured pilot and that the comparison was valid.
State that the conversion increase was five percentage points rather than five percent.
items.because: The distinction matters.

items.says: Clarify the scope of “all merchants.”
items.because: It is unclear whether this means all merchants in the product, market, or company.

items.says: Consolidate this experiment with the later checkout A/B-test bullet.
items.because: The later bullet repeats the same accomplishment.

items.says: The RICE bullet is mostly a process statement without an outcome.
items.because: It does not identify a resulting roadmap decision, launch, or business impact.

items.says: Clarify whether support tickets were a valid proxy for affected users.
items.because: Reach was scored as the number of tickets each feature would close.

items.says: Combine this bullet with the next roadmap bullet if they describe the same process.
items.because: The two bullets overlap.

items.says: “Set the next quarter's roadmap priority” is too vague.
items.because: It does not say what changed or happened afterward.

items.says: Clarify whether leadership approved the recommendation, a feature was built, or measurable savings followed.
items.because: The current result does not establish the recommendation's impact.

items.says: The long sequence of activities obscures the decision and its significance.
This bullet overlaps with the RICE prioritization bullet.
items.because: Both appear to describe the same roadmap process.

items.says: Verify that session-level randomization was appropriate.
items.because: The same user may have encountered both experiences depending on the implementation.

items.says: Distinguish the unit of analysis, experiment population, and affected party.
items.because: Reporting the result as an effect on merchants' customers is potentially imprecise.

items.says: This bullet repeats the checkout-conversion accomplishment without adding a business outcome.
items.because: The same experiment is already described earlier.

items.says: Remove this as a standalone bullet unless rigorous experimentation detail is relevant to the target role.
Include statistical significance or confidence information only if it can be accurately supported.
Clarify what “funded” means.
items.because: It could mean approved budget, engineering capacity, or formal rollout authorization.

items.says: Update the “Present” date if the project or app is no longer active.
Clarify whether this was an operating product, student venture, or classroom project.
items.because: The distinction affects how recruiters evaluate the results.

items.says: State the current level of involvement if the project continues.
Clarify what the 3,100 students represent.
items.because: They could be registered users, eligible students, notified students, or total reach.

items.says: Clarify what “with two dining halls” means.
items.because: It is unclear whether the app served the halls or the halls supplied the food.

items.says: Verify how the nine tonnes of food were measured.
items.because: The amount may have been weighed directly or estimated.

items.says: Define the start and end dates of the first-year period.
The stated 150% increase is incorrect.
items.because: An increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%.

items.says: Clarify the before-and-after measurement periods.
Verify the implied causal link between the 60 interviews and the reminder-feature decision.
items.because: “Chosen after 60 user interviews” implies that the interviews directly established the feature choice.

items.says: The stated 20% increase is ambiguous.
items.because: Moving from 75% to 95% is a 20-percentage-point increase or about a 26.7% relative increase.

items.says: Clarify whether the volunteer shift system was a product intervention, an operational process, or both.
Add the measurement period for the fill-rate change.
Make the practicum's academic context clear.
items.because: The project occurred during the MBA rather than as professional employment.

items.says: Distinguish the candidate's personal contribution from the team's work.
items.because: “Team Lead” does not by itself identify individual contributions.

items.says: Clarify whether the $2.4 million was a modeled opportunity, forecast, or validated savings estimate.
items.because: The distinction between estimated and realized savings should remain clear.

items.says: Add implementation timing, adoption status, or pilot-budget context if available.
items.because: It would make the client outcome more concrete.

items.says: The bullet is passive and primarily describes work performed rather than impact.
Quantify the reduction in form length, intake time, errors, or staff burden.
items.because: No measurable improvement is stated.

items.says: Clarify whether all four clinics adopted the changes and whether adoption was approved or merely observed.
Make the candidate's individual role in the mapping or redesign clearer.
Avoid redundancy with the $2.4 million pilot bullet if both describe the same approval process.
Clarify whether the pilot launched or was only approved.
items.because: The bullet should not imply implementation if only approval was received.

items.says: The product-skills section is too short and generic for a product-management application.
Separate discovery, experimentation, analytics, and delivery skills if supported.
items.because: More specific categories would better communicate the candidate's capabilities.

items.says: The A/B-testing skill needs support from accurate experiment-design knowledge.
items.because: The résumé raises questions about session-level randomization and measurement.

items.says: “Requirements writing” is too broad.
items.because: The résumé does not identify the types of artifacts produced.

items.says: Relevant demonstrated capabilities are missing from the skills section.
items.because: The résumé also shows stakeholder management, process improvement, forecasting, vendor management, change management, and financial modeling.

items.says: The tools section is underdeveloped.
Add analytics, SQL, presentation, documentation, or experimentation tools if substantively used.
The listed tools lack evidence elsewhere in the résumé.
items.because: Recruiters may test claimed tool proficiency.

items.says: Excel is not very differentiating on its own.
items.because: It is not paired with specific analytical or modeling capabilities.
